Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary The game Select a group of connected tokens of the same color to pop them. (Tokens are only connected orthogonally, not diagonally.) You must pop at least two tokens per turn - singles can't be popped. White tokens are wild and can be used as any color; you must select another color along with white. The goal is to have none of your secret color tokens remaining on the board: if this happens you win instantly. Otherwise, the game ends when there are no longer any tokens that can be popped, at which point the player with the least remaining of their color on the board wins. (Ties go to the player who popped the fewest tokens of their own secret color.) It is important to note having popped the most of your own color is not a winning condition. When a column is emptied, all of the columns are slid together to close the gap. Variants Two secret colors : this variant allows you to play Color Pop with two secret colors, which will have you thinking very often on which color you are gonna favor this turn! This variant is only available for two player games. Game preferences The colorblind option available for this game enables an alternative setup displaying symbols on the tokens using the great color code designed by Miguel Neiva: ColorADD . [Rating: 2/10] I was so bored during the 5 minutes the game lasted. Maybe if you really love match-3 games. Not for me.

[Rating: 2.5/10] The game plays best online. Pieces stick. It's colorful, its a good idea. It's good for people who like these kinds of apps. The thing is, it just doesn't translate well into a board game. It's a good idea but it's just better as an app or a video game. meh.

[Rating: 2.7/10] Geez, not sure about this one after playing a number of games online. It just seems random and abstract with little skill involved. I also get frustrated playing this game for some reason and it does not seem to be much fun. I am not actually sure there is even a game in there, or maybe it is just me that is missing something.

[Rating: 3/10] Well, this one is tricky: I really like the mechanism how this game is made, but now you need just experienced game developer to make the game, which uses the board better way. Now there is very little game in here.

[Rating: 3/10] A board game implementation of the pop-the-same-colour-groups computer games that have existed in countless variations for the last decade. Almost sure to be pointlessly chaotic in multiplayer games. Nice discs maybe.  Thrifted on 11/11 2015 and 9/9 2017.

[Rating: 3/10] Fun mechanism to play, but the refilling is way too bothersome. I'd rather play this with my phone

[Rating: 3/10] Never thought I'd see an analog match 3 game, but here it is! Some clever solutions here. Still, I don't think it improves the digital game enough to make it worth it.

[Rating: 3/10] it will be better as a computer game. not very interesting and engaging as a board game.

[Rating: 3/10] Dull. Unlike the puzzle this is based on, this one is ruined by other people getting in the way :)

[Rating: 3/10] Nothing really to this game.  Pop random colours and try to have the least of yours remaining.  There's not a lot you can do to salvage your colours or hinder your opponents.  It's also very obvious within a few turns which colour each person is going for.
